name: ssh-copy-id
description: Installs your public key on a server's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys — the one-command setup for key-based login.

examples.explanation: Prompts for the password ONE LAST TIME, then installs your default public key. From now on, ssh user@server needs no password.
Installs a specific key on a server using a custom port.

about: ssh-copy-id appends the public key to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server with correct permissions (700 dir, 600 file) — permissions that manual copying frequently gets wrong, which is why "key auth not working" is such a common problem.
useCases: Set up key authentication on new servers.
Roll out a new key to a fleet of machines.
mistakes: Manually creating authorized_keys with wrong permissions instead of using ssh-copy-id.
Copying the private key to the server by mistake.
